standard_prerequisites.name: Skeleta and their induction
standard_prerequisites.statement: The n-skeleton sk_n V of a simplicial object and its induction i_{n!} sk_n V, with the canonical map to V.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the objects of the colimit in the statement (source lines 3807-3811).

standard_prerequisites.name: Degreewise stabilisation and injectivity
standard_prerequisites.statement: In degree m the n-skeleton of V agrees with V for n at least m, and the transition maps between successive induced skeleta are injective (the author's lemma-n-skeleton-abelian, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: They give both the colimit identification and the injectivity claim (source lines 3815-3818).

core_obligations: Identify the colimit: use that in each degree m the n-th skeleton equals V once n is at least m, so the colimit of the induced skeleta is V (source lines 3815-3817).
Record injectivity: cite the skeleton lemma for the injectivity of the transition maps (source lines 3817-3818).

proof_roadmap.step: Show degreewise that the colimit of the induced skeleta is V.
Cite the skeleton lemma for injectivity of the transition maps.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-abelian-limit-skeleta at source lines 3804-3812: in an abelian category every simplicial object V is the colimit of the induced skeleta i_{n!} sk_n V, with all transition maps injective. The proof at source lines 3814-3819 is a one-line degree argument: in degree m the n-th skeleton already agrees with V as soon as n is at least m, which identifies the colimit with V, and the injectivity of the transition maps is the cited skeleton lemma. It is the tersest item in this half of the chapter, but the argument given is the actual reason and reduces the claim to the cited lemma.
